info.title: Reading and changing code
info.text:
High-level code uses readable words and structures.

Readable code is usually easier to understand and change.

Low-level code requires more knowledge of the processor.

Challenge: Why might a high-level language help staff update a quiz each week?

Maintenance includes correcting and changing a program. High-level languages usually reduce the effort needed.

info.title: Development time
info.text:
High-level operations can express a task in fewer instructions.

Low-level code often needs more detailed instructions.

More detailed code can take longer to write and check.

Challenge: Why can high-level code reduce development time?

Development time is the time spent creating the program. It is different from the time the finished program takes to run.

info.title: Moving to another system
info.text:
High-level source is usually more portable.

The new system needs a suitable translator.

Low-level code is tied more closely to a processor.

Challenge: Why may low-level code need rewriting for a different processor?

Portability does not mean every source program works unchanged on every device. Compare the language levels using the requirement given.

info.title: Control of hardware
info.text:
Low-level code closely matches processor operations.

It allows detailed control of hardware and memory use.

This control comes with greater development effort.

Challenge: Why might low-level code suit a routine needing precise hardware control?

A strong answer explains why detailed hardware control matters to the stated task.

info.title: Speed and memory
info.text:
Low-level code can be carefully tuned for a processor.

This can help control execution speed and memory use.

High-level code usually makes development easier.

Challenge: A tiny routine must use little memory. Give one benefit and one drawback of low-level code.

Avoid claiming low-level code is always faster. Its relevant advantage is the detailed control it can give a programmer.

info.title: A justified recommendation
info.text:
Identify the main requirement in the project.

Choose the language level that addresses it.

Explain both the benefit and a relevant drawback.

Challenge: Recommend a level for a school app that needs frequent changes on several systems.

Use the scenario to decide which characteristics matter. There is no single language level that is best for every task.
